title: The smoker
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: The uncle smokes the grunion in a rusted oil drum behind the shack. Alder. The smoke goes across the launch and the strip draws it as the only soft line in the run. Gully tends it. The uncle supervises from the pot.

panels.composition: Behind the shack: a rusted oil drum on blocks, smoke pouring from a gap in its lid, GULLY feeding alder chips. The UNCLE on his pot. WOOD, BARNABY.

image.prompt: a rusted oil drum smoker on blocks behind a shingle shack pouring pale smoke, a teenager feeding wood chips, an old man seated on a crab pot, a young man and a dog, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The smoke. Drawn soft — the only soft line the strip allows itself this year.

image.prompt: close on pale smoke rising and drifting from a drum's lid, rendered in soft lines, black and white, no words

balloons.text: Alder. Not cedar. Cedar's for roofs.

image.prompt: an old man on a crab pot speaking without moving, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The launch in smoke. The shack a shape. The three and the dog, shapes. The smoke goes across the bay and the strip goes with it.

image.prompt: a boat launch and shack softened by drifting smoke, figures and a dog reduced to shapes, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: 'Then why'd I say it.' The only soft line of the year.
